posts.name: Mohan Siva Sanjay Bhimaneni
posts.cooked:
Below is a PPA from week 5:

Given a shell variable month supposed to contain a string value corresponding to some calendar month. Use the cal command to create a file named as X.txt where X is the string value in the variable month. Your command should also create a file named error.txt that should contain the error message if the string month does not correspond to any calendar month. Create all the files in the current working directory.

For example:

  1. If the variable month contains the string “nov”, your solution should create a file named nov.txt containing the calendar of november month and error.txt should be empty.
  2. And if the variable month contains the string “garbage”, your solution should create a file named error.txt containing the error from cal command and garbage.txt should be empty.

Here are the test case results of a correct solution:

image244×434 6.8 KB

The year is wrong, since the test cases were old. I had to change the date of the system to get this right.
I request you to please keep the test cases up to date so that we do not have to face such technical problems.
Thank you..

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
This is not a configuration issue Mohan.

You can output the calendar of any month and any year, without changing the date of the system. The question tests your ability to debug, and read the documentation to find the solution.

I would urge you to explore how to solve this purely by using the date command with appropriate arguments.

Regards,
Sayan

posts.name: Mohan Siva Sanjay Bhimaneni
posts.cooked:
That is true, and not my point.
I am sorry for the miscommunication. I did not mean the system date has to be changed, I had to add an extra argument “-d 2023-01” to the cal command to get the test cases right.
Also, the question did not mention any details about the specific year to be displayed, so people assume it is the present year. So, all I am asking is to include the year in the question, or change the test cases
